placeholder_rlc.description: Fixed RLC-pi equivalent (2.895nH per half, center-tapped), carried over verbatim from opensubghz's sky130_fd_pr__ind_05_125 -- NOT a real GF180MCU inductor model. Split out as its own block (a/b/ct/sub interface) specifically so a real characterized/EM-extracted model can be added later as a sibling topology sharing the same interface, without touching whatever instantiates sch/inductor.sym.

ind_03_90.description: sky130_fd_pr__ind_03_90's own characterized RLC-pi equivalent (760.5pH per half, center-tapped) -- NOT a GF180MCU model either, added purely to compare against the ind_05_125 placeholder currently in use for the VCO tank.

ind_05_220.description: sky130_fd_pr__ind_05_220's own characterized RLC-pi equivalent (4.96nH per half, center-tapped) -- NOT a GF180MCU model either, added purely to compare against the ind_05_125 placeholder currently in use for the VCO tank.

spiral.description: Real GF180MCU octagonal spiral, characterized by a 3D FDTD (openEMS) run instead of a carried-over reference RLC-pi. Renamed from 'spiral_openems': openEMS is this topology's current FITTING METHOD, not its identity -- the topology itself is 'an octagonal GF180MCU spiral inductor'. 'schematic' is now a normal STATIC template (inductor_spiral.sch, discrete L/R/C symbols with 'l'/'rs'/'cox'/'rsub'/'csub'/'cs' substitute_params() tokens) like every other topology -- inductor_spiral_generator.py's fit_electrical_params() (invoked host-side by resolve_generator_params() at materialization time, or in-container after a real FDTD run) supplies those 6 derived values, declared in parameters_file's derived_parameters.generator block. No center-tap/mutual-coupling EM model yet (single continuous 2-terminal winding, planar port + Metal4 crossunder bringing both terminals adjacent) -- rsub/csub/cs are placeholder-quality until a real center-tap-aware EM methodology exists. See openems_inductor_status.md project memory for the port-topology history and open issues (Q sign/magnitude still under investigation as of this entry).
references: sch/inductor/inductor_spiral_generator.py -- this repo's own generator, invoked by mh-analog-designer's run_sim.py (resolve_generator_params() for the fast placeholder path, run_one_openems()/openems_generator_runner.py for the real FDTD path)

loop.description: Simple rectangular closed-loop GF180MCU Metal5 inductor, characterized by a 3D FDTD (openEMS) run -- formalizes tools/gf180mcu_inductor_diag_loop.py's own already-validated standalone diagnostic (single planar in-line port bridging a gap cut into one side, extracted R within 5% of the analytic estimate) as a real generator-backed topology, using the SAME generator contract and the SAME pi-network circuit model as 'spiral' (inductor_spiral.sch copied verbatim to inductor_loop.sch). Only 3 free geometric parameters (width_um, height_um, track_width_um -- no turns/spacing, no crossunder/center-tap EM model) -- deliberately simpler than 'spiral', meant as an independent, already-validated reference for exercising the openEMS materialize/FDTD/fit workflow while 'spiral' still has an open Q-sign bug (see openems_inductor_status.md).
references: sch/inductor/inductor_loop_generator.py -- this repo's own generator, same materialize/run contract as inductor_spiral_generator.py
tools/gf180mcu_inductor_diag_loop.py -- the standalone diagnostic this topology formalizes

spiral_diff.description: Octagonal, center-tapped, DIFFERENTIAL GF180MCU spiral inductor -- a genuine Y-branch of two mirror-image wound arms sharing node 'ct' (unlike 'spiral'/'loop', each a single continuous 2-terminal winding with no second magnetically-distinct arm). Layout/geometry done and approved; characterized by 3 SEPARATE single-port FDTD (openEMS) runs (an 'open/short-circuit transformer test': arm A alone, arm B alone, full structure with arm B's far end shorted to ct) rather than one run -- a direct single-port measurement bridging the two arms' far-terminus pads directly was found methodologically invalid for this topology (adds an artificial short-cut path instead of measuring the real ct-mediated winding, and can never reveal mutual coupling since an open secondary carries no current by definition). See inductor_spiral_diff_generator.py's own module docstring for the full derivation, pi_model_fit.py's fit_mutual_inductance()/assert_mutual_inductance_recovers_synthetic() for the combining math (validated against synthetic data), and tools/gf180mcu_spiral_diff_mutual_fit.py for the offline 3-run combiner. The .sch template extends inductor_loop.sch's pi-network with one new element: a SPICE K mutual-coupling statement between L1/L2, driven by a new 'k_coupling' derived parameter -- physically meaningful here (unlike 'loop'/'spiral') because the two arms really are separate windings. build_openems_structure() REQUIRES geometry['variant'] in {'arm_a','arm_b','shorted'} (raises otherwise) -- there is no automatic single-run real-FDTD path for this topology through the normal materialize flow; a real characterization is always the 3-run offline combiner. See spiral_diff_bringup_status.md project memory for the full bring-up trail.
references: sch/inductor/inductor_spiral_diff_generator.py -- this repo's own generator (geometry_from_params/build_openems_structure/fit_electrical_params, same contract as inductor_loop_generator.py, but build_openems_structure() takes a required geometry['variant'])
tools/gf180mcu_spiral_diff_mutual_fit.py -- offline 3-run combiner (cache-only, no Docker/CSXCAD needed), same spirit as tools/gf180mcu_inductor_refit.py

quadrature_lc.description: Quadrature LC-VCO: two cross-coupled NMOS negative-gm cores (half_qvco_cell), each with its own LC tank, tail-coupled via an extra injection pair driven by the other core's differential output -- forces the two cores into quadrature lock. Ported from opensubghz's SKY130 half_qvco_param/vco_transfer_tb (nfet3_01v8 -> nfet_03v3, cap_var_lvt -> cap_nmos_03v3 MOS varactor). Runs on its own vco_vdd rail (3.3V, matching nfet_03v3's rating) rather than the chip's 5.0V analog rail. Inductor is a placeholder RLC subckt carried over verbatim from opensubghz -- not a real GF180MCU inductor model; pending rnxrbb's own inductor characterization work.

quadrature_lc_cascode1.description: Cascoded variant of quadrature_lc: each half-cell's cross-coupled pair (M1/M2) gets a cascode device (M6/M7) stacked between it and the tank/injection nodes, isolating the tank from M1/M2's own finite output conductance. Added after loop_gain sweeps on quadrature_lc showed that, at minimum channel length, the bare cross-coupled pair's own gds cancels out most of its useful -gm/2 negative conductance, so scaling W/current on the plain pair alone could not close the loop against the placeholder inductor's loss (Q~11). Cascode gate bias (nbias2) comes from a second diode-connected reference M2, stacked in series ABOVE M1 (same shared ibias current flows through both) -- a replica-biasing scheme mirroring the real signal path's own M6/M7-over-M5 stack, rather than a fixed voltage.
references: opensubghz's SKY130 half_qvco_param/vco_transfer_tb (nfet3_01v8 -> nfet_03v3, cap_var_lvt -> cap_nmos_03v3 MOS varactor)

etspc_d2d3.description: Extended True Single Phase Clock (E-TSPC) divide-by-2/3 prescaler, two cascaded classic Vaucher-style 2/3-cells (JSSC 2000 'A Family of Low-Power Truly Modular Programmable Dividers...') built from nfet_05v0/pfet_05v0 (GF180MCU 5V thick-oxide devices, this block's own 5.0V 'vdd' rail rather than the VCO's 3.3V vco_vdd). 'sw' is a single external bit that couples the two cells' own modulus-control paths together (via MW0), shifting the WHOLE block's overall division ratio by one step when toggled -- see tb/divider/tb_divider_funct.py, which MEASURES the actual ratio for each 'sw' level rather than assuming which level means which ratio (not yet confirmed against a real simulation). KNOWN GAP: etspc_d2d3.sch's own PFET sources (M1/M3/M6/M9/M12/M15) are not yet tied to any 'vdd' net, even though sch/divider.sym already reserves a 'vdd' pin for this topology -- the schematic cannot simulate correctly until that wiring is added (in the xschem GUI, where pin/wire coincidence can be checked visually) alongside a decision on whether the symbol's separate 'SUB' pin is actually needed by these devices or is unused copy-paste from the VCO's own hierarchical symbol template.
references: C. Vaucher et al., 'A Family of Low-Power Truly Modular Programmable Dividers in Standard 0.35-um CMOS Technology', IEEE JSSC, July 2000 (E-TSPC 2/3-cell reference topology)

Measured division ratio (steady-state output period / input clk period) -- informational, see the 'ratio error' metric for the actual pass/fail check. Confirmed by a real simulation (2026-09-14, clk_freq=1.05e9, tt/25) that sw=0 gives exactly 2 (ratio_error ~7e-8); sw=5.0 (vdd) unexpectedly ALSO measured 2, not the assumed 3 -- open issue, see the topology's own config.json description and the MW0/modulus-control wiring.

Deviation of the measured division ratio from its own nearest integer -- the real functional-correctness check (should be ~0 regardless of which 'sw' level/ratio a given run is; a miscounting divider shows up here as a large, non-integer ratio instead)
Output duty cycle (steady-state, informational)

Output duty cycle's deviation from the ideal 50% -- cycle asymmetry matters beyond aesthetics here: in the real PLL this divider feeds a delta-sigma-modulated dual-modulus chain, and a duty-cycle/delay difference BETWEEN the 'sw' states (compare this metric's value across the sw=0 and sw=5.0 conditions) shows up as a periodic disturbance synchronized with the modulator's own switching pattern -- a fractional-spur mechanism, not just a cosmetic imbalance.

Average VDD power over the last few steady-state output periods (v(vdd)*i(vdd) averaged over a real transient window, not a bare .op point -- see this topology's own config.json description for why a DC operating point has no meaningful consumption figure for a clocked dynamic circuit)

Net conductance at resonance (Re(Y11); negative = net negative resistance, oscillation should grow -- positive = net loss, matches a decaying tb_startup kick)
